\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Majority binomial factorization]
\lean{FABL.majority_binomial_factorization}
\label{FABL.majority_binomial_factorization}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $m$ and $j$ with $j\le m$, 
\[
\frac{\binom{m}{j}^{2}\binom{2m}{m}}{\binom{2m}{2j}}=\binom{2j}{j}\binom{2(m-j)}{m-j}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Exact majority Fourier weight formula]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_two_mul_add_one_eq_limiting_mul}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_two_mul_add_one_eq_limiting_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierCoeff_majority_two_mul_add_one, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_eq_choose_mul, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_eq, FABL.majority, FABL.majority_binomial_factorization, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence}
\difficulty{6}
For natural numbers $m,j$ with $j\le m$, the level-$(2j+1)$ Fourier weight of majority
on the sign cube of dimension $2m+1$ equals
$\lambda_{2j+1}\,\frac{\pi}{2}(2m+1)I_{m-j}I_m$, where $I_q=\binom{2q}{q}/2^{2q}$ and
$\lambda_k=\frac{2}{\pi}a_k$ for odd $k$, with $a_k=\frac{2}{k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Lower bound for the majority influence factor]
\lean{FABL.one_le_majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor}
\label{FABL.one_le_majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddMajorityInfluence, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceMain, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceMain_le, FABL.oddMajorityInfluenceMain_sq, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_pos}
\difficulty{5}
For natural numbers $m$ and $j$ with $j\le m$, let $I(r)=\binom{2r}{r}/2^{2r}$ for each
natural number $r$. Then $1\le (\pi/2)(2m+1)I(m-j)I(m)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Even-index influence bound]
\lean{FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_sq_le_even}
\label{FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_sq_le_even}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddMajorityInfluence, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_sq_le}
\difficulty{3}
For every integer $m>0$, let $I_m=\binom{2m}{m}/2^{2m}$. Then $I_m^2\le
\dfrac{2}{\pi(2m)}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Majority influence factor bound]
\lean{FABL.majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor_le_rpow}
\label{FABL.majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor_le_rpow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.oddMajorityInfluence, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_pos, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence_sq_le_even}
\difficulty{6}
For natural numbers $m$ and $j$ with $j<m$, let $I(r)=\binom{2r}{r}/2^{2r}$ for each
natural number $r$. Then
\[
\frac{\pi}{2}(2m+1)I(m-j)I(m)\leq\left(1-\frac{2j+2}{2m+1}+\frac{2j+1}{(2m+1)^2}\right)^{-1/2}.
\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Limiting weight bounded by majority Fourier weight]
\lean{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le_fourierWeightAtLevel_majority}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b001
}
\label{FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_le_fourierWeightAtLevel_majority}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_two_mul_add_one_eq_limiting_mul, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_pos_of_odd, FABL.majority, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence, FABL.one_le_majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers, with both $n$ and $k$ odd and $k\le n$. The limiting
majority Fourier weight at level $k$ is at most the total Fourier weight at level $k$ of
the majority function on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier weight bound for odd majority]
\lean{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_le_limitingMajorityFourierWeight}
\label{FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_le_limitingMajorityFourierWeight}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.exercise5_24, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel_majority_two_mul_add_one_eq_limiting_mul, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight, FABL.limitingMajorityFourierWeight_pos_of_odd, FABL.majority, FABL.majorityFourierWeightLimitFactor_le_rpow, FABL.oddMajorityInfluence}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be odd positive integers with $2k<n$. The level-$k$ Fourier weight of
majority on the $n$-dimensional Boolean cube is at most $(1+2k/n)$ times the limiting
majority Fourier weight at level $k$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p123-b006}
\difficulty{5}
For each odd positive integer $k$, let $W_k(r)$ be the sum of the squared level-$k$
Fourier coefficients of majority on the cube $\{-1,1\}^{k+2r}$, using the uniform
measure. As $r\to\infty$, $W_k(r)$ converges to $\frac{2}{\pi}a_k$, where
$a_k=\frac{2}{k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{4}
For each odd positive integer $k$, let $W_k(r)$ be the sum of the squared level-$k$
Fourier coefficients of majority on the cube $\\{-1,1\\}^{k+2r}$, with Fourier
coefficients taken as expectations under the uniform measure. Then $W_k(r)$ is strictly
decreasing in $r$ and converges, as $r\to\infty$, to $\frac{2}{\pi}a_k$, where
$a_k=\frac{2}{k2^k}\binom{k-1}{(k-1)/2}$.
\end{theorem}
